facts: The paper studies how to make loss-aware predictions in image segmentation settings where the evaluation function is the Intersection-over-Union (IoU) measure.
The Intersection-over-Union (IoU) measure is used widely in evaluating image segmentation systems.
There are two dominant approaches currently.
One approach approximates the Expected-IoU (EIoU) score as Expected-Intersection-over-Expected-Union (EIoEU).
Another approach computes exact EIoU but only over a small set of high-quality candidate solutions.
The authors ask which approach should be favored for two typical image segmentation tasks.
The study leads to two new methods.
The two new methods draw ideas from both existing approaches.
The new methods use the EIoEU approximation paired with high quality candidate solutions.
Experiments show that the new approaches lead to improved performance on both image segmentation tasks.
The first dominant approach approximates the Expected-IoU (EIoU) score.
The second dominant approach is to compute exact EIoU.
EIoU is an abbreviation of Expected-IoU.
In the studied settings, the evaluation function is the Intersection-over-Union (IoU) measure.
entities: loss-aware predictions in image segmentation settings
